phrase.text: Calling a subprogram means pausing what you are doing, running the subprogram with its arguments and coming back exactly to where you paused.

runs.text: Calling a subprogram means pausing what you are doing, running the subprogram with its arguments and coming back exactly to where you paused.
A call writes the name and, inside required parentheses, the arguments. The arguments are computed
from left to right and only once
, and must match the parameters in number and type.
: a space of its own for its parameters and local variables. When it ends, the frame disappears and control goes back to the caller.

blocks.description: A stack with the Principal frame at the bottom. Calling Doble pushes a frame with n = 21; on return it disappears and the value 42 goes down to Principal.

caption.text: Frames are stacked when calling and removed when returning. Only the top one is running.

runs.text: A subprogram that returns a value is used
, where a value is needed. One that returns nothing is used
. Mixing them up has different consequences:

rows.text: using as a value something that returns nothing
calling as a statement something that returns a value

points.text: Parentheses are required; arguments are computed from left to right.
Number and types must match the signature.
Every call has its own frame, which disappears on return.
Discarding a returned value is a warning.
